source.title: Il catechismo di don Giuseppe Sarto, Arciprete di Salzano

methodology: Checked the Museo San Pio X Italian web transcription at all 24 chapter-specific numbered-Q&A loci; source line and question ranges are provided separately.
The modern editor supplied sequential question numbers, did not transcribe numbers originally written by Sarto; these are editorial locators only.
Page carries later interpretation and facsimile captions interleaved with Sarto's dialogue. No editorial commentary or later opinions are adopted as purported Sarto original utterances.
Source-aligned context candidates are not verified whole replies, literal quotation mappings, approved translations or pre-approved model evidence.
Personal moral verdicts, sacramental validity decisions, modern disciplinary exceptions, unproved speculative or universal claims are held.
A separate fidelity/alignment pass must verify each admitted question's exact source support before gate admission. Existing 144-node research gate is unchanged.

importantEditorialTextWarnings.location: Confirmation section around printed 445–447; web page line about 1880
importantEditorialTextWarnings.issue: The webpage prints 406 where the numbered sequence suggests 446; do not silently rewrite the manuscript or confuse numbering with original autograph.
Capitalized narrative judgments about Sarto's teaching and comparisons to later thinkers are editor's interpretation, not manuscript Q&A.
Historic fasting and ministry regulations must not be presented as present-day canonical prescriptions.
The online account describes 252 autograph revisions, but these revisions were not personally checked against physical manuscript folios.

sourceLoci.attestedTopicParaphrase: The divine Son assumed human body and soul in the Incarnation, for the work of redemption.

sourceLoci.attestedTopicParaphrase: The passage explicitly teaches future bodily resurrection and judgment, not mere continued memory.
